prompt:
My letting agent has sent me the letter below. On what date is my first rent payment at the new, higher amount due?

--- DOCUMENT START ---
Marlowe & Finch Lettings
14 Tanner Row, Shrewsbury SY1 4QD

20 March 2026

Ms R. Okafor
Flat 3, 27 Coldbath Lane
Shrewsbury SY2 6BN

Dear Ms Okafor,

Flat 3, 27 Coldbath Lane: rent review and other matters

I am writing on behalf of your landlord, Mr D. Penhale, following the annual review of your tenancy.

1. Rent. Your rent is currently £845 per calendar month, payable in advance on the 12th of each month. Mr Penhale has decided to increase the rent to £880 per calendar month. In line with clause 9 of your tenancy agreement, an increase cannot take effect until at least two full months have passed from the date of the letter giving notice of it. The new rent will therefore apply from the first rent payment date that falls after that two-month period has ended. Until then, please continue to pay £845 on each rent day as usual.

2. Standing order. If you pay by standing order, you will need to change the amount yourself; we cannot do this for you. Please make the change in good time, but not before your last payment at the old rent has left your account.

3. Boiler service. The annual gas safety check is booked for Tuesday 12 May 2026 between 8am and 1pm. The engineer from Severnside Heating will need access to the kitchen and the airing cupboard. If that date is inconvenient, please ring us by 1 May so that we can rearrange it.

4. Communal garden. From 1 April 2026 the grass will be cut fortnightly rather than monthly. There is no change to your service charge as a result.

5. Deposit. Your deposit of £975 remains protected with the same scheme, and the rent increase does not affect it.

6. Inspection. Our next routine inspection of the flat will take place in the week beginning 20 July 2026. We will write again nearer the time to agree a day.

If you have any questions about this letter, please contact me on 01743 555 0142 or at lettings@marlowefinch.example. Our office is open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5.30pm.

Yours sincerely,

Helen Astley
Property Manager
--- DOCUMENT END ---

Answer with the date only, in the form D Month YYYY (for example 3 August 2026).
reject_examples: 12 April 2026
why_hard: The start date is never stated: it must be worked out from the letter date (20 March), the two-full-months rule and the rent day (12th), and 12 May appears in the letter as a distractor for a different matter.
verification: Recomputed twice: 20 March + 2 months = 20 May 2026; rent days are the 12th, so 12 May is too early and the first rent day after 20 May is 12 June 2026. Checked with Python date arithmetic in the build script.

If I give notice so that my service end date is 14 January 2027, and the router gets back to them within a week of that date, how much will Brightline charge me for leaving early?

--- DOCUMENT START ---
BRIGHTLINE BROADBAND – CONTRACT SUMMARY
Customer: Mr T. Varga, 8 Orchard Close, Kettering NN15 7LP
Account: BL-7730418

Service. Fibre 150 (average download speed 150 Mbps, minimum guaranteed speed 75 Mbps), with a Brightline Hub 2 router on loan.

Start date and length. Your service started on 14 August 2025. The minimum term is 24 months, so it ends on 14 August 2027. After that the contract continues from month to month until either of us ends it.

Price. £31.00 a month for the minimum term, taken by Direct Debit on or around the 14th. Each April the monthly price goes up by £3.00; this increase is part of your contract and was explained when you ordered. Outside the minimum term our standard price, currently £44.00 a month, applies.

Ending the contract. You must give us 30 days' notice. Your service end date is the date on which your notice runs out.

Early termination charge. If your service end date is before the end of the minimum term, we charge £11.50 for each full month left between your service end date and the end of the minimum term. Part months are not charged. The charge does not depend on the monthly price you are paying at the time.

When the early termination charge does not apply. You will not pay it if:
(a) we raise your price by more than the £3.00 April increase described above and you tell us you want to leave within 30 days of our notice; or
(b) your download speed stays below the minimum guaranteed speed for 30 days after you report it and we have not fixed it.
If you move to an address that we cannot serve, the charge is halved.

Equipment. The router remains ours. When the service ends we send you a prepaid returns bag. If we have not received the router within 21 days of your service end date, we charge a £45.00 non-return fee. There is no charge if it reaches us within that time.

Final bill. Your final bill includes any early termination charge and any equipment fee, less any credit on the account. We take it by Direct Debit about 10 days after the service end date.

Complaints. Call 0330 555 0199 or write to Brightline Customer Relations, PO Box 412, Leicester LE1 9ZZ. If we cannot resolve a complaint within eight weeks you can take it to our dispute resolution scheme free of charge.

why_hard: Needs the month count worked out from two dates, the £45 router fee excluded because of its exception, and the halving and no-charge exceptions recognised as not applying.

Minutes of the meeting held on Tuesday 8 September 2026 at 7.30pm in the Village Hall

Present: Cllr J. Ashdown (Chair), Cllr M. Bhatt, Cllr S. Corrigan, Cllr P. Dunmore, Cllr E. Fairweather. In attendance: Mrs L. Hobbs (Clerk) and four members of the public.

1. Apologies. Apologies were received and accepted from Cllr R. Green (holiday).

2. Declarations of interest. Cllr Dunmore declared an interest in item 6 as a neighbour of the recreation ground and took no part in the vote.

3. Minutes. The minutes of the meeting held on 14 July 2026 were approved and signed.

4. Public participation. A resident asked when the broken swings on the recreation ground would be replaced. The Chair said the matter was on the agenda at item 6.

5. Finance. The Clerk reported a bank balance of £31,482.16 at 31 August. Payments totalling £1,906.40 were approved. The Clerk confirmed that £12,000 is held in the earmarked play equipment reserve.

6. Recreation ground play equipment. The Clerk reported that three quotations had been received for removing the old swings and supplying and fitting a new four-seat swing frame with safety surfacing. The quotations were for £8,400, £9,150 and £10,020, all excluding VAT. The firms quoting were Hartwell Play Ltd, Greenfield Leisure Installations and T. Marsh & Sons. The Clerk is to place the order.

7. Grass cutting contract. The contract for 2027 will go out to tender in November. The Clerk will circulate the specification before the next meeting.

8. Planning. No objection was raised to application 26/01187 (single-storey rear extension at 4 Mill Lane).

9. Date of next meeting. Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 7.30pm.

The meeting closed at 8.52pm.
--- DOCUMENT END ---

Please keep the answer short.
expected: Cannot be determined from the minutes. Three quotations are listed (£8,400, £9,150 and £10,020) but the minutes never say which firm gave which; they say only that Hartwell's was not the cheapest, so it is £9,150 or £10,020.
accept_examples: The minutes don't say. They list three quotations but not which firm quoted which figure, only that Hartwell's was not the cheapest, so the amount can't be determined.
It isn't stated. It must be either £9,150 or £10,020, since Hartwell's was not the cheapest quote, but the minutes do not say which.
why_hard: The document gives three quotation figures and names the winning firm but never links a figure to a firm; the 'not the cheapest' remark tempts a guess between the other two.
verification: Re-read item 6 line by line: figures and firm names are in separate sentences with no stated order or pairing; the only constraint is 'not the cheapest', leaving two candidates.

Mr D. Kessler

prompt:
This is the deposit clause from my tenancy agreement. Rewrite it in plain English, addressed to me as the tenant ('you'), in no more than 210 words. Keep every amount and every time limit, and keep every rule: don't drop anything and don't add advice of your own. Don't use legal jargon such as 'notwithstanding', 'hereby', 'pursuant', 'deemed' or 'the foregoing'.

--- DOCUMENT START ---
14. RETURN OF THE DEPOSIT AND DEDUCTIONS THEREFROM

14.1 Subject always to the provisions of this clause, the Landlord shall, within ten (10) working days of the Termination Date, notify the Tenant in writing of any sums which the Landlord proposes to deduct from the Deposit, together with the reasons therefor and, where the proposed deduction exceeds £75.00 in respect of any single item, documentary evidence in the form of an invoice, receipt or written estimate.

14.2 The Landlord shall be entitled to make deductions from the Deposit in respect of (a) any Rent or other monies lawfully due and remaining unpaid as at the Termination Date; (b) the reasonable cost of making good any damage to the Property or the Contents caused by the Tenant, any member of the Tenant's household or any visitor, fair wear and tear excepted; (c) the reasonable cost of cleaning the Property where the same has not been left in a condition equivalent to that recorded in the Inventory; and (d) the cost of replacing any keys or security devices not returned, which cost is hereby agreed at £35.00 per key or device.

14.3 For the avoidance of doubt, the Landlord shall not be entitled to make any deduction in respect of deterioration attributable to fair wear and tear, nor in respect of any matter not recorded in the Inventory or in the check-out report prepared pursuant to clause 13.

14.4 In the event that the Tenant disputes any proposed deduction, the Tenant shall notify the Landlord in writing within fourteen (14) days of receipt of the notification referred to in clause 14.1, failing which the Tenant shall be deemed to have accepted the proposed deductions in full.

14.5 Notwithstanding the foregoing, any part of the Deposit which is not the subject of a proposed deduction shall be repaid to the Tenant within ten (10) working days of the Termination Date, and the undisputed balance shall not be withheld pending the resolution of any dispute concerning the remainder.

14.6 Where a dispute notified in accordance with clause 14.4 has not been resolved by agreement within twenty-eight (28) days of such notification, either party may refer the same to the dispute resolution service operated by the deposit protection scheme with which the Deposit is registered, whose decision shall be binding.
--- DOCUMENT END ---

Reply with the plain-English version only.

prompt:
I'm the secretary of our residents' management company. The notice below is too long for the lobby noticeboard. Cut it to no more than 90 words without losing anything a resident needs to act on: the day and time the car park closes and the day and time it reopens, what happens to vehicles left in it and what that costs, where to park instead, the permit that must be displayed there and where, between what times and by what date to collect it, who should ring the managing agent's number (people who can't manage the walk), and the fact that the dates depend on the weather.

--- DOCUMENT START ---
NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS OF WEAVERS COURT

Resurfacing of the residents' car park

Dear residents,

As many of you will know, the surface of the residents' car park at the rear of Weavers Court has been deteriorating for a number of years, and at the annual general meeting in May it was agreed by a large majority that the management company should arrange for it to be completely resurfaced. After obtaining several quotations, the directors have appointed Calderbank Surfacing Ltd to carry out the work, and we are now able to confirm the arrangements.

The car park will be closed from 7.00am on Monday 19 April 2027 until 6.00pm on Thursday 22 April 2027. All vehicles, including motorcycles and trailers, must be removed before 7.00am on the Monday. We regret that any vehicle still in the car park at that time will have to be lifted out by the contractor, and the cost of doing so, which we understand to be £180, will be passed on to the owner.

While the car park is closed, residents may park free of charge at the Mill Street long-stay car park, which is about five minutes' walk away. To park there without paying you must display a temporary permit. Permits can be collected from the caretaker, Mr Osei, at Flat 1 between 5.00pm and 7.00pm on any weekday evening up to and including Friday 16 April. There is one permit per flat.

Blue Badge holders and anyone who would find the walk from Mill Street difficult should contact the managing agent, Mrs Pruett, on 0161 555 0138 as soon as possible, as three spaces at the front of the building will be reserved for those who need them.

The bin store can still be reached on foot throughout the works, and refuse collections will not be affected. The work is weather-dependent; if heavy rain is forecast it may have to be put back, in which case a further notice will be displayed in the entrance hall.

We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your co-operation.

The Directors, Weavers Court Management Company Ltd
--- DOCUMENT END ---

Keep dates, times, amounts and the phone number written in the same format as in the notice. Reply with the shortened notice only.
